title: ai_rate_limiter plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `ai_rate_limiter` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component AiRateLimiterConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

AiRateLimiterConfig.description: Plugin: ai_rate_limiter — HTTP-only token-aware rate limiting for LLM APIs. Native gRPC is unsupported (not registered for the Grpc protocol view): protobuf message frames have no supported usage schema, so an attachment there would never charge the budget. Framed gRPC-Web bodies are likewise never classified as JSON AI traffic and are never charged as zero usage. Pre-dispatch prompt estimates walk the request JSON once, counting billable string values, visited object member names (including tool/function schema property names), and JSON scalar literals at serialized width so a present recognized field cannot suppress unknown billed text; exclusions are path/context aware (unsigned numeric output caps only at the exact paths also read for completion-budget reservation — negative/fractional values count fail-closed; multimodal URL/base64/file leaves only inside matching provider content-part family and part type — member names and unrelated textual siblings still count; wrong-family/malformed parts and ordinary strings including data: URLs in instructions/schemas always count). The estimate weights each character by its UTF-8 width (ASCII at chars/4 as before; two-byte scalars such as Cyrillic or Greek at two per token; CJK, kana, Hangul, Indic, and emoji at one token each) and adds media_token_estimate per recognized image/audio/file part; it is a reservation heuristic, not provider tokenizer parity. Only identified AI calls (or POST bodies it cannot inspect) consult the budget: GETs, framed gRPC-Web, and parsed non-LLM JSON are never refused or counted. Every uncompressed POST is classified from its bytes whatever its Content-Type label, and a body a request transform turns into an AI call is re-classified and admitted at the final request-body stage. Budget refusals (429) carry Retry-After. Supports centralized Redis-backed mode for cross-instance token budget coordination. Counter storage supports only local memory and Redis; database-backed counters are intentionally unsupported. When Redis is unavailable at terminal reconciliation, actual usage is charged locally within the existing identity cap and the reservation lifecycle is finalized, including zero-token reservations and committed streams. Successful fallback sets instance-scoped ai_ratelimit_locally_accounted=true. Local usage is not replayed to Redis. Process counters ferrum_ai_rate_limit_local_accounting_tokens_total and ferrum_ai_rate_limit_unaccounted_tokens_total expose fallback charges and capacity-limited accounting gaps. Admission remains fail closed; buffered/federated successful responses still receive 503 and committed streams retain their response.

token_limit.description: Required maximum tokens allowed per window. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer. Omission is rejected at construction; there is no default.

window_seconds.description: Sliding window duration in seconds. Capped at 2678400 (31 days) so the window stays representable as a monotonic duration and a signed Redis TTL.

expose_headers.description: Inject x-ai-ratelimit-* headers. For successful buffered metered responses, usage and remaining reflect the bucket after provider-usage reconciliation (not the admission estimate). Limit and window stay coherent with the configured budget. Unmetered charge_estimate keeps the reservation; warn releases and refreshes; reject substitutes a 502 that still carries all four headers, describing the retained reservation, because the rejection-path after_proxy publishes this instance's telemetry onto the final response. Only the centralized enforcement-unavailable 503 carries no rate-limit headers, because no authoritative counter could be consulted. Non-2xx and gateway-rejection releases refresh to the post-release bucket. Federation reconciles before header copy on the rejection-path after_proxy.

provider.description: LLM provider format for token extraction. Accepted values: auto, openai, anthropic, google, cohere, mistral, bedrock, tgi. The constructor trims surrounding Unicode whitespace and lower-cases the value, so `" OpenAI "` is accepted and normalizes to `openai`; the pattern above admits exactly those spellings and no others. Gemini/Vertex payloads use `google`; Hugging Face TGI native `/generate` and `/generate_stream` shapes use `tgi`, whose authoritative counter is `details.generated_tokens` (TGI's OpenAI-compatible surface stays `openai`).

on_unmetered_response.description: Action for successful responses without usage metadata. charge_estimate keeps the pre-request reservation, reject returns a 502 and keeps the reservation (the 502 carries the x-ai-ratelimit-* headers when expose_headers is on), warn logs and releases the reservation. On a STREAMED response the headers are already committed, so reject cannot substitute a 502; it degrades to its fail-closed accounting half (the reservation stays charged) and logs the violation.

consumer_limits.description: Per-consumer token ceilings, keyed by mapped Consumer username (requires limit_by consumer). An unmapped external identity never matches, even one that spells a listed username. A listed consumer keeps its own window; only the ceiling differs. Unlisted consumers, external identities, and IP-keyed fallbacks use token_limit.

model_limits.description: Per-model token budgets, keyed by the request body's exact top-level `model`. A request for a listed model is charged against that model's own window per identity, with this ceiling, and never against the default window; a model budget takes precedence over consumer_limits. Unlisted models use the default budget. While model_limits is set, an AI candidate whose model cannot be read before dispatch is refused (415 with Accept-Encoding identity for a still-compressed body, 400 for an unparseable one). A request transform that changes model re-attributes the reservation to the final model's budget.

media_token_estimate.description: Tokens pre-reserved for each recognized image, audio, or file content part (the parts whose binary payload the prompt estimate excludes). 0 reserves nothing for media; reconciliation still charges the provider-reported usage.

sync_mode.description: Token budget storage: 'local' (in-memory) or 'redis' (centralized), parsed case-insensitively (`LOCAL`, `Redis`). `redis` additionally requires `redis_url`. Database-backed counters are unsupported. Any RESP-compatible server works.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL (e.g., redis://host:6379/0), required with sync_mode=redis. The database selector is a canonical decimal integer from 0 through 2147483647, without signs, zero-padding, or extra slashes. An absent path or bare slash selects database 0. Ferrum uses the portable signed-32-bit bound; redis-rs represents indexes as i64. The server separately checks its configured databases on SELECT. TCP port range is constructor-validated. URL fragments are forbidden; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for all Redis keys. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:{plugin_name}:{plugin-config-id}` so two independent policies of this plugin type in one namespace do not share counters. Setting this explicitly is the documented opt-in for a deliberately shared budget: every instance configured with the same prefix increments and rejects against the same counters.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_failure_policy.description: Behavior when the centralized Redis store cannot be consulted: an outage, an egress/DNS screen failure, or an endpoint rejected as an unsupported topology (Redis Cluster is not supported). fail_closed refuses the request with 503 and no rate-limit headers; local_fallback explicitly opts into per-process budgets, which enforce the configured limit once per gateway process. Only meaningful with sync_mode=redis, but validated in either mode.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Redis connection timeout in seconds. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer.
